result.text: Title: Luxury Airplane You produce airplanes.
While the base model is always the same, your customer likes to pimp their airplane with fancy interior.
You let them decide between a number of 5 different bars, the number of seats, their color, and the amount of water in the toilets of their plane (you can come up with additional stuff).
After you received the specifications you send the requirements to different teams to manufacture the parts.
E.g.
manufacturing the vodka bar is done by the Russian team, the whiskey bar is manufactured by an Irish team.
After receiving the individual bits and pieces, the interior of the plane is assembled, and the plane is sent on a test flight.
During the flight you create a test protocol which is sent to you and the customer.
The plane is delivered to the customer, which has to confirm.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Give the outgoing sequence flows of an event-based gateway no conditionExpression; the first occurring target event selects the path.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.

args.text: When a process description says that a participant chooses one option from several alternatives, model the choice with an exclusive gateway and route each option to its corresponding activity using conditional sequence flows.

trace.reason: Check whether an already learned guideline states this same modeling rule.

result.rule: When the description presents mutually exclusive alternatives selected according to a stated condition: model an exclusive gateway to route the process into the applicable alternative, with outgoing flows reflecting the stated conditions

When the description says that an event or milestone can change the route during work, or that completion makes follow-up actions available: Model the supported outcomes as connected conditional branches, using a suitable gateway for the stated choice; when flow waits for an event or other trigger, model the wait with an intermediate catch event.

When the description states a sequence of activities or a conditional step followed by a later activity: Connect the activities and any modeled gateways in the stated order with sequence flows, including every described transition.

When the description says an optional activity may occur after an outcome, and each occurrence is followed by another specified activity: Model the optional activity as a task on one branch of an exclusive gateway, with the other branch ending or continuing as described; connect the activity back to the specified later activity when it must follow each occurrence.

args.text: When modeling activities and gateways, use labels that faithfully describe the actions and decisions stated in the process description; do not add unsupported details or change their meaning.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already covers faithful BPMN labels.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.

args.text: When labeling BPMN activities and gateways, use concise wording that preserves the specific action or decision stated in the process description; do not replace it with a broader, narrower, or different meaning.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers faithful BPMN labels.

result.rule: When the description distinguishes an event or activity by its action, actor, object, recipient, or another meaningful qualifier: Label each BPMN element so that it preserves those stated details without substituting a broader or different meaning.

When the description states a specific action, decision, or outcome, but a generated BPMN element label expresses a different meaning: Label the element to preserve the meaning of the corresponding described step; do not substitute another action, decision, outcome, or an inferred purpose.
When the description specifies an activity’s object, recipient, or other meaningful qualifier: Preserve that qualifier in the BPMN task label rather than replacing it with a broader paraphrase.

When the description gives an activity or decision a meaningful qualifier, such as its recipient, scope, timing, or eligibility criteria: Preserve meaningful qualifiers in the BPMN task label or gateway question; do not broaden or narrow the stated action or decision.
